parsed.explanation: No trans-specific offence, facility ban or documented police/border targeting; same-sex conduct decriminalised Dec 2022 via constitutional court. Visitor-facing protections are largely undocumented, public facilities/custody/care unknown. The sole documented trans violence is dated 2018 with a 2019 sentence of $460/no jail for a meat-cleaver throat attack, signalling impunity. Official and religious hostility toward LGBT people is documented, alongside Pride/vigils, a pro-LGBT prime minister and church opposition to the former buggery law. Resident employment exclusion and family non-recognition are climate signals only. Overall: no universal exposure, but thin recourse and hostility keep it below reduced-risk anchors.

federal_state_facilities.interaction: One island-wide regime; no subnational variation documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Official/religious LGBT hostility, state questioning LGBT migration legitimacy; no trans-specific offence documented and same-sex conduct decriminalised 2022.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Constitutional decriminalisation and high-court anti-discrimination ruling; prime minister reported pro-LGBT.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Hostile framing coexists with court-led decriminalisation; no documented enforcement against trans presentation.

minors_guardians.interaction: Former serious-indecency provision unresolved; no trans-specific minor/custody findings.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Single 2018 meat-cleaver attack on trans activist causing serious throat injuries; trans residents reportedly fired/denied jobs for dressing wrong (resident sphere).
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Conviction without jail ($460 or 3 months) evidences impunity outcome; no later documented instance, so dated signal.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Employment act excludes gender identity/expression; no visitor-service remedy documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Regional commission case filed 2018, unresolved after 2022 decriminalisation.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of documented remedies for trans violence/services is not safety; resident gaps do not offset.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: no active sexuality-law enforcement and some social visibility. Lower than 0.65-C because no established gender-diverse community role or documented compensation remedy, and documented impunity sentencing plus stronger official hostility.

Similar elevated tier: no universal ban or police targeting, but weak/incomplete remedies. Higher than 0.55-A because decriminalisation is complete and no recurring visitor-facing service refusals are documented.
Higher than this case: 0.75-C has documented ordinary respect, identity-based facilities/wards and enforced court compensation. This dossier documents none of those visitor-facing positives.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime is island-wide with no documented local variation. Decriminalisation removes the main sexuality-law lever, and no tier-1 universal exposure or organised targeting is documented. Interaction is between hostile state/religious framing and a court that decriminalised, visibly organised trans activism, and a lenient sentencing outcome for serious violence. Undocumented entry, facilities, custody and care cannot be treated as safe; they remain open questions. The dated impunity case and absence of working visitor remedies place the case in elevated risk, above jurisdictions with unremedied bans or targeting but below those with documented acceptance and enforced protections.
